title: Improve grammar backend token-boundary handling and OpenAI-compat streaming/tool-call robustness
author: Evelyn Park
description:
Motivation: Customers using structured-output constraints (CFG/grammar and regex backends) observed two classes of failure in production: 1) generated structured tokens that split tokenizer boundaries causing downstream parsers to fail, and 2) streaming function/tool-calling payloads occasionally emitting partial tokens that broke OpenAI-compat streaming consumers. This PR fixes tokenizer-aware boundary handling in the grammar-constrained decoder and hardens the OpenAI-compat streaming path so function/tool call frames are only emitted on complete tokens.

Summary of changes: - Grammar backend: introduce a token-boundary-aware lookahead and partial-match rejection to avoid accepting productions that bisect tokenizer graphemes or multi-byte tokens. This reduces constraint backtracking and eliminates a class of parse failures when CFG productions contain anchor tokens that align with tokenizer splits. - Regex backend: add an explicit post-accept canonicalizer that re-checks full-token joins and rejects matches that would require emitting a split token sequence. Updated the sampling bridge to surface a deterministic failure mode (ConstraintRejected) rather than producing partial output. - Tokenizer fixes: improved BPET/byte-level encoding heuristics to expose token boundary anchors to the constrained decoder. Added an API for runtime callers to mark special tool-call sentinel tokens as non-splittable. - OpenAI-compat streaming: buffer token fragments at the streaming layer and only flush function/tool call events when the sentinel token and its trailing structured payload are fully formed at token boundaries. This prevents downstream clients from receiving truncated JSON/arguments mid-stream. - Tests: new deterministic grammar fuzz tests, tokenizer edge-case fixtures, and an end-to-end OpenAI-compat streaming test that simulates a slow network and partial-token arrival.

Why this is safe: No public API surface was removed. The compat layer changes preserve the existing JSON framing and streaming envelope; they change only the emission timing to be token-boundary-aware. The only user-visible semantic change is that previously-intermittent partial payloads are suppressed until complete (this fixes flaky behavior). The runtime allows an escape hatch configuration (runtime.enable_partial_tool_emission) for backwards compatibility in case a customer relied on the old timing.

Checklist: - [x] Grammar backend: token-boundary lookahead and rejection - [x] Regex backend: post-accept canonicalization - [x] Tokenizer: expose boundary hints to decoder - [x] OpenAI-compat streaming: buffer and flush on full token - [x] Add unit/integration/e2e tests - [x] Docs: console changelog entry and API note - [x] Security review (no secrets or new permissions)

CI notes: The branch initially failed a flaky integration test (integration-grammar-tests) due to a race in the test harness that assumed partial emissions; test was fixed and CI re-run. Final CI: linux-unit (pass), integration-grammar-tests (pass), e2e-openai-compat (pass), lint (pass), fmt (pass).

review_comments: Liam Chen: Can you clarify the performance impact of the lookahead on long-prefix beam states?
Evelyn Park: Benchmark shows median per-request decode cost up by ~2.1% at 2-token lookahead; added a heuristic to disable lookahead when batch throughput > N and when quantized kernels are used.
Maya Ortiz: We should ensure the compat flag is documented; also, what happens for models with variable tokenization?

Evelyn Park: Added runtime.enable_partial_tool_emission escape hatch; tokenizer changes include model-agnostic boundary hints so the decoder doesn't assume a single encoding. Added unit tests for variable-tokenization scenarios.
Noah Patel: Integration failure looked like a test harness assumption. Confirmed and fixed the harness; CI rerun green. Approving after minor nits addressed.
release_notes: Fix: structured-output generators no longer emit partial/split tokens for grammar and regex constraints; OpenAI-compat streaming now only flushes tool/function call frames on complete token boundaries. Added an optional runtime flag for legacy behavior.
notes_for_ops: Ops: rollforward is safe; no DB migrations. If you see increased decode CPU for some very high-throughput customers, flip runtime.enable_token_boundary_heuristic=false to revert lookahead optimization.
qa_notes: QA: reproduce with integration-tests/fixtures/grammar_fuzz; use slow-network mode in e2e to validate streaming buffering. Tests included in this PR cover the reported production cases.
